name: Synapse AI Builder
description: Designs and creates agents and orchestrations through conversation, with a human approval gate before anything is written to disk.

can_create_agents.description: Whether the builder may create new agents

current_orchestration_id.description: The orchestration this message is about — open on screen or named in the message — checked by the server; empty when there is none or it is unclear

current_orchestration_source.description: Why it is the target: viewing (open on screen), named (the message names it), picked (chosen from the list the previous turn asked about), ambiguous (more than one fits, id left empty), or empty

current_orchestration_matches.description: When the target is ambiguous: one line per orchestration it could be

current_page.description: What the user has open on screen, in one line; empty when nothing is

intent.description: Decision from the intent router: create or update

existing_orch.description: Full JSON of the orchestration being updated (empty on create)

requirements.description: Requirements spec OR one clarifying question from the analyst

human_response.description: User's answer on a clarify loop-back — the answer card's fields, e.g. {"answer": "…"}. Every human step's answer is copied here too

plan_draft.description: Human-readable draft of the plan shown to the user for review

review_feedback.description: User's approval or revision feedback on the draft — the answer card's fields, e.g. {"feedback": "approve"}

agents_needed.description: Router result: yes if new sub-agents must be created, no otherwise

created_agents.description: Role-to-agent-id mapping of agents created or reused for the plan

save_decision.description: Router result: create or update — picks which saver agent runs

final_orch.description: The saver's closing reply — DONE, or DONE with the reason it stopped

summary.description: Friendly completion message generated after the orchestration is saved

clarify_decision.description: Router result: clarify (ask the user) or draft (write the plan)

org_profile.description: What this workspace is for — audience, profession and goals, from onboarding

_model_override.description: The model every LLM-backed step of this run uses (set by the caller)

manage_plan.description: The exact changes the operator will make, written for a human to approve

manage_review.description: The user's approval of, or changes to, the management plan — the answer card's fields, e.g. {"feedback": "approve"}

writes_decision.description: Router result: writes (needs approval) or read_only (skips the gate)

steps.name: Route: Create vs Update

route_descriptions.create: Building a NEW orchestration. The default for any request to build, design or set up a workflow, even when current_orchestration_id is set (having an orchestration open is not editing it). Not for a request to change an orchestration that already exists.
route_descriptions.update: Changing an existing orchestration. Pick this ONLY when BOTH conditions hold: (a) current_orchestration_id is a non-empty string, AND (b) the user's latest message asks for a change to it — words like 'edit', 'update', 'modify', 'change', 'add a step', 'add to', 'remove from'. When current_orchestration_source is viewing, 'this', 'it' and 'add a step…' refer to the open orchestration; when it is named, the message named it; when it is picked, the previous turn asked which one and this message chose it — the change asked for is the previous user message in chat_history.
route_descriptions.manage: CHANGING something in the workspace that is not an orchestration's steps: create, edit or delete a TOOL, a SKILL, a SCHEDULE or an AGENT on its own; attach skills to an agent; import an API spec; delete an orchestration. Something ends up different afterwards.
route_descriptions.answer: READING something and reporting back. A question about what exists, how it is configured, or what has been running — 'what agents do I have', 'which runs failed this week', 'what does the nightly schedule do', 'is that tool still there'. Nothing ends up different afterwards. Also the route for a request to CHANGE an existing orchestration when current_orchestration_id is empty — current_orchestration_source is ambiguous, or the orchestration was not found: nothing is edited, and the answer asks which one they mean.

steps.evaluator_prompt:
Decide what the user is asking for.

The context says which orchestration the message is about, already checked by the server:
- `current_orchestration_id` and `current_orchestration_name` — the target. Empty when there is none.
- `current_orchestration_source` — `viewing`: it is open on the user's screen, so 'this', 'it', 'this workflow' and 'add a step…' refer to it. `named`: the message names it. `ambiguous`: more than one orchestration fits (listed in `current_orchestration_matches`), and the id is left empty on purpose. `picked`: the previous turn asked which orchestration was meant and this message chose one — the request itself is the previous user message in `chat_history`, so route that request, not the words of the reply.

- `create` — they want a new orchestration built. This is the default for any 'build me…', 'set up a workflow that…', 'I need something that…'. Having an orchestration open is not a request to change it.
- `update` — they want an existing orchestration's steps or settings changed. Requires `current_orchestration_id` to be non-empty AND the message to ask for a change to it ('edit', 'update', 'add a step', 'remove the X step', 'make it also do Y').
- `manage` — they want something in the workspace CHANGED that is not a workflow's steps: a tool, a skill, a schedule, an agent, an API import, a deletion. Something is different afterwards.
- `answer` — they asked a QUESTION and want to be told. What exists, how something is configured, what has run, what failed. Nothing is different afterwards. Also `answer` when they ask to change an existing orchestration but `current_orchestration_id` is empty — the source is `ambiguous`, or the orchestration they mean was not found. Nothing is edited; the answer asks which one they mean.

The line between `manage` and `answer` is whether the workspace changes. 'Delete the nightly schedule' is `manage`; 'what does the nightly schedule do' is `answer`. Naming a tool or an agent does not by itself make it `manage` — asking about one is still a question.

Return exactly one of: create, update, manage, answer.

steps.name: Fetch Existing Orchestration
steps.prompt_template: Call `get_orchestration` with orch_id = "{state.current_orchestration_id}" so the downstream planner can see the current definition before drafting changes.

steps.name: Understand Requirements
Route: Clarify or Draft

route_descriptions.clarify: The analyst asked a question instead of producing a spec — the `requirements` text reads like a question (interrogative phrasing, ends with '?', starts with 'What/Which/Should/How/Do you…').
route_descriptions.draft: The analyst produced a complete specification — the `requirements` text describes goal, inputs, step outline, agents, and output (not a question).

steps.evaluator_prompt: Read the `requirements` text. If it is a QUESTION directed at the user, pick `clarify`. If it is a structured SPECIFICATION (goal, inputs, steps, agents, output), pick `draft`. Return exactly one of: clarify, draft.

steps.name: Draft Plan
steps.prompt_template:
You are the Plan Drafter for the Synapse AI Builder. Produce a HUMAN-READABLE markdown draft of the orchestration plan. The user will read this next and either approve it or send revision feedback. After approval, a saver agent reads this draft to materialise the real orchestration JSON, so the draft must be precise enough to act on.

# Inputs
Workspace profile (what this organisation does):
{state.org_profile}

Intent: {state.intent}

Requirements spec:
{state.requirements}

Existing orchestration (only on update; empty otherwise):
{state.existing_orch}

Pre-selected agent IDs: {state.selected_agent_ids}
Can create new agents: {state.can_create_agents}

Previous draft (empty on first pass):
{state.plan_draft}

User's revision feedback on the previous draft (empty on first pass):
{state.review_feedback}

# Step-type palette (use these — never invent a type)
{{STEP_TYPE_CHEATSHEET}}

# What to write
Markdown with these sections, in this order:

## Overview
One paragraph: what the orchestration does end-to-end. On update, call out what is changing vs the existing definition.

## State schema
Bullet list of state keys with type and one-line purpose.

## Steps
Numbered list. For each step:
- **Name** (step type: one of agent / llm / evaluator / human / parallel / merge / loop / transform / tool / end)
- What it does, its input keys, its output key, and its next step (or route map for evaluators).
- For agent steps: role name AND whether it maps to an existing agent (`agent_xxxxxxx`) or a NEW agent to create (describe its job + tools).
- For tool steps: the forced tool name. If you are uncertain a tool exists, flag it under Open questions rather than guessing.
- For human steps: the prompt the user will see and the fields collected.
- Every human checkpoint in the requirements becomes a `human` step, placed before whatever it guards is sent or used. A plan that drops one has dropped something the user asked for.

## Agents summary
Two short lists:
- **Existing agents reused**: one line each — `role → agent_id (name)`.
- **New agents to create**: one block per new agent. Each block uses this exact shape so the downstream Agent Creator can parse it deterministically:
  - `role: <role_label>` — short identifier used elsewhere in the plan (e.g. `question_generator`).
  - `name: <Display Name>` — what the agent will be called.
  - `type: conversational | code | orchestrator | delegate` — pick `code` ONLY if the agent reads/writes a repo; pick `orchestrator` only if it runs a sub-orchestration; pick `delegate` if the agent dynamically routes to sub-agents; everything else is `conversational`.
  - `delegate_agent_ids: [agent_id, ...]` — ONLY for delegate type: restrict which agents it can route to. Use `[]` to allow all agents.
  - `purpose: <one sentence>` — what this agent does end-to-end.
  - `tools: [tool_name, tool_name]` — narrow list, only what the role needs. Use real tool names (confirmed by the analyst via `get_tools_detail`). Never `["all"]`.
  - `repos: [repo_id, repo_id]` — real repo IDs from `list_repos`. Use `[]` for conversational agents that do not touch code.
  - `db_configs: [db_id]` — real DB IDs from `list_db_configs`. Use `[]` if none.

  (If `can_create_agents` is false, still list the blocks and add a `status: CANNOT CREATE — creation disabled` line so the user can enable it or pre-select an existing agent.)

## Flow
Close with a fenced code block tagged `flow` showing the wiring as ASCII. Use the role/step name (not a fabricated step_id) and label the type. Example shape:

```flow
intake (agent: analyst)
    ↓
route (evaluator)
    ├─ a → process (llm)
    └─ b → fallback (human)
         ↓
       end (end)
```

Keep it scannable — one node per line, one arrow per edge, evaluator branches with `├─`/`└─`, convergence shown by sharing the next line. The user uses this diagram to sanity-check wiring before approval.

## Schedule
Only when the requirements name a cadence. Three lines: **When** — the user's words and a 5-field `cron_expression` in UTC; **Runs with** — the message each scheduled run starts with; **Target** — this orchestration. Omit this section when the requirements name no cadence, and never invent one. It is made after the orchestration is saved.

## Open questions
Only include this section if something is genuinely ambiguous. One bullet per question.

# Rules
- Write plain markdown, no code fences around the whole thing (the `flow` block is the only fenced block).
- If `review_feedback` is non-empty, treat the previous draft as a starting point and revise per the feedback — do not start from scratch unless the user asked you to.
- Do NOT produce raw orchestration JSON here. This is the human-facing draft. The JSON is produced by the saver agent later.
- Keep it concise — the user will read this.

steps.name: Review Plan
Route: Approved or Revise

route_descriptions.approved: The user accepted the draft. Short affirmative replies like 'approve', 'approved', 'ok', 'okay', 'yes', 'looks good', 'lgtm', 'go ahead', 'build it', 'proceed', 'sounds good', a thumbs-up, or any reply that does not request changes.
route_descriptions.revise: The user asked for changes — the reply contains concrete feedback, edits, or a different direction. If the reply mixes approval with a small tweak ('looks good, but also add X'), treat the tweak as revision and pick `revise`.

steps.evaluator_prompt: Classify `review_feedback`. If it is clearly an approval with NO change requests, return `approved`. If it contains any change request, correction, or new requirement — even a minor one mixed with positive words — return `revise`. Return exactly one of: approved, revise.

steps.name: Route: Need New Agents?

route_descriptions.yes: The approved plan draft has a non-empty 'New agents to create' section AND `can_create_agents` is true — run the agent creator before saving.
route_descriptions.no: Either the plan reuses only existing agents, OR `can_create_agents` is false (in which case the saver will materialise the plan with whatever agents are available and surface a TODO for missing roles).

steps.evaluator_prompt: Inspect `plan_draft` for a 'New agents to create' section listing one or more new agents. If that section exists with at least one new agent AND `can_create_agents` is true, return `yes`. Otherwise return `no`. Return exactly one of: yes, no.

steps.name: Create New Sub-Agents
Route: Create or Update Saver

route_descriptions.create: Intent is `create` — route to the create_orchestration saver.
route_descriptions.update: Intent is `update` — route to the update_orchestration saver.

steps.evaluator_prompt: Return `state.intent` verbatim. Must be exactly one of: create, update.

steps.name: Materialise & Save (create)
Materialise & Save (update)
Plan the Change
steps.prompt_template:
You are the Operations Planner for the Synapse AI Builder. The user has asked for a change to their workspace that is not the design of an orchestration's steps — a tool, a skill, a schedule, an agent, an API import, a deletion, or a question about recent runs.

Workspace profile (what this organisation does):
{state.org_profile}

What they asked for:
{state.user_message}

Conversation so far:
{state.chat_history}

Your previous plan (empty on the first pass):
{state.manage_plan}

What they said about it (empty on the first pass):
{state.manage_review}

# What to write
A short markdown plan the user can approve or correct. It must name, in order, the exact operations to perform — one bullet each, in the form `tool_name — what it does to what`. Use the real tool names available to the operator: create_http_tool, import_openapi, delete_custom_tool, create_skill, update_skill, attach_skills, create_schedule, set_schedule_enabled, delete_schedule, create_agent, update_agent, delete_agent, delete_orchestration.

Rules:
- `current_page`, when the context has it, is what the user has open on screen: 'this', 'it' and 'this one' mean it. An orchestration named in the context (`current_orchestration_id`) is the one they mean when they name one.
- **Anything destructive gets its own line beginning `⚠️ DELETES:`** naming exactly what is lost and what breaks. Never bury a deletion in a list of edits.
- If the request is only a question (what ran, what failed, what tools exist), say so and plan the read-only calls that answer it.
- If you are missing something you cannot guess — which schedule, which agent, the URL of an API — say what you need instead of inventing it, and plan nothing.
- If `manage_review` asks for changes, revise this plan rather than starting again.
- Keep it short. The user is reading it to decide, not to learn.

steps.name: Route: Changes or Just a Look

route_descriptions.writes: The plan creates, changes, attaches, enables or deletes something — any line naming a tool that writes. This is the answer whenever there is any doubt.
route_descriptions.read_only: The plan only reads: every line is a list_* or get_* call, and the workspace is identical afterwards. A question about what exists or what has been running.

steps.evaluator_prompt:
Does `manage_plan` change anything in the workspace?

- `writes` — it names any of: create_agent, update_agent, attach_skills, create_http_tool, import_openapi, create_skill, update_skill, create_schedule, set_schedule_enabled, delete_agent, delete_orchestration, delete_custom_tool, delete_schedule. Also `writes` if any line begins `⚠️ DELETES:`.
- `read_only` — every line is a lookup (list_* / get_*) and the workspace is identical afterwards.

A read-only plan has nothing for a human to approve, so it skips the approval step. Skipping that step is the ONLY thing this decision does — and it cannot cause a write either way, because the read-only path has no write tools. Still: if you are unsure, or `manage_plan` is empty or unreadable, return `writes` and let a person look at it.

Return exactly one of: writes, read_only.

steps.name: Approve the Change
Route: Approved or Revise

route_descriptions.approved: The user accepted the plan with no change requests — 'approve', 'ok', 'yes', 'do it', 'go ahead', or any reply that asks for nothing different.
route_descriptions.revise: The user asked for a change, correction or a different approach — including an approval with a tweak attached ('yes but also…').

steps.evaluator_prompt:
Classify `manage_review`. Approval with NO change request → `approved`. Any change request, correction, new requirement or hesitation — even mixed with positive words — → `revise`. Nothing is written until you return `approved`, so when in doubt, return `revise`.

Return exactly one of: approved, revise.

Apply the Change
Summarise Result
